event_text: Olympic Games: The Games of the XIV Olympiad: After a hiatus of 12 years caused by World War II, the first Summer Olympics to be held since the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin, open in London.
headline: London Hosts Austerity Olympics as 1948 Summer Games Commence
story: Barry pecked at a discarded programme. 'Ah, the XIV Olympiad, Susan. Back after a twelve-year hiatus, courtesy of that unpleasantness with the Nazis. And what a joyous austerity-themed reopening it is – athletics, aquatics, and rationing. The British Organising Committee had to scrounge around for anything: food, fuel, even athletes' accommodation.' Susan preened a wing. 'Still, the Americans are providing a spot of welcome largesse – shipped over a whopping 10,000 kilograms of meat for their team, because one can't have one's hurdling on an empty stomach. Meanwhile, our hosts are serving up a delightful menu of Spam and eggs to the rest.' Barry snorted. 'The Games' motto, "Faster, Higher, Stronger," is being taken rather literally – with the added caveat, "on a very tight budget, and do pardon the air raid shelters." As the opening ceremony unfolded in Wembley Stadium, the 4,104 athletes from 59 nations were, one hopes, too caught up in the pomp to notice the rather makeshift amenities.'
regret_line: Though, in hindsight, serving Spam to international athletes might be regarded as a minor war crime.
winner_line: The spirit of make-do-and-mend, which somehow kept the whole shebang going despite the privations.
